questions.stem: Why is the concentrated hydrochloric acid added in small portions?

options.text: Each portion builds pressure that must be vented by opening the stopper before the next addition
options.explanation: Portioning plus venting keeps the gas release controlled and safe.

options.text: Because the alcohol only reacts with exactly 3 cm3 doses
options.explanation: The reaction proceeds with any dosing; portioning is a safety practice.

options.text: To keep the funnel cold
options.explanation: Cooling is not the purpose of portioning.

options.text: To dissolve the alcohol faster
options.explanation: Dissolution is not the rate-limiting concern here.

options.text: The product itself, selectively
options.explanation: The wash targets acids, not the chloride product.

options.text: Acidic impurities from the organic layer
options.explanation: The hydrogencarbonate neutralises residual acid left from the reaction mixture.

options.text: Water dissolved in the organic layer
options.explanation: Water removal is the drying agent's job.

options.text: The unreacted alcohol
options.explanation: Unreacted alcohol stays with the organic layer and is separated by distillation.

questions.stem: Magnesium sulfate is added to the organic layer to

options.text: Catalyse the chlorination reaction
options.explanation: The reaction is already complete by this stage.

options.text: Colour the product for identification
options.explanation: No colouring role exists.

options.text: Bind traces of water so the liquid turns clear before distillation
options.explanation: The anhydrous sulfate hydrates, scavenging water from the product.

options.text: Neutralise acidic impurities
options.explanation: That is the hydrogencarbonate wash's role.

questions.stem: The distillation collects the fraction between 47 and 53 degrees because

options.text: The product melts in that range
options.explanation: Melting belongs to solids; this product distils as a liquid.

options.text: The thermometer reads that range only
options.explanation: The thermometer reads any range; the collection is a choice.

options.text: The impurities cannot vaporise at all
options.explanation: They vaporise at other temperatures, which is why the window excludes them.

options.text: The product boils in that window, so collecting only there excludes lower and higher boiling impurities
options.explanation: The bracket around the product's boiling point is the identity check of the distillation.

questions.stem: Why does this concentrated-acid synthesis demand a fume hood?

options.text: Concentrated hydrochloric acid releases hydrogen chloride gas rapidly whenever it is uncovered
options.explanation: The toxic, irritant fumes must be drawn away before they reach the laboratory air.

options.text: The alcohol is radioactive
options.explanation: No radioactivity is involved.

options.text: The product is explosive
options.explanation: The product is a volatile liquid, not an explosive.

options.text: Distillation requires a draught to work
options.explanation: Distillation works by heating and condensing, not by draught.

questions.stem: State the volumes and conditions used at the start of this synthesis.
questions.modelAnswer: 8 cm3 of 2-methylpropan-2-ol meets 20 cm3 of concentrated hydrochloric acid added in 2-3 cm3 portions inside a fume hood.

questions.stem: State the distillation range collected for the product.
questions.modelAnswer: The distillate is collected between 47 and 53 degrees, the bracket around the product's boiling point.

questions.stem: Explain why the funnel is stood for 20 minutes with shaking at intervals before the layers are separated.
questions.modelAnswer: The acid-alcohol substitution needs sustained contact to reach completion, so the standing time with periodic shaking lets the reaction proceed while the mixing keeps fresh acid in contact with the alcohol layer.

questions.stem: A student forgets the hydrogencarbonate wash and distils the dried organic layer directly. State which impurity survives into the distillate and why the collection window may not exclude it.
questions.modelAnswer: Dissolved acidic impurities such as hydrogen chloride survive, because they dissolve in the organic phase and some co-distil near the product's boiling range, so the window alone cannot exclude chemically dissolved impurities that a wash would have removed.
